newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks start lower in line with Wall Street.
newsitem.headline: French stocks start lower in line with Wall Street.

text.p: French shares opened lower on Wednesday in line with Wall Street, after a 66-point overnight fall in the Dow Jones Industrial Index but the Paris market showed more resistance than the U.S. market, dealers said.

The French blue-chip index opened 0.43 percent down while Wall Street posted a 0.96 percent fall on late jitters over Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan's second part of his testimony on the economy to Congress tonight.
A stronger dollar and German data showing a slightly better economy underpinned French shares, which were but a whisper away from their all-time high on Tuesday, dealers said.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index was down 13.71 points or 0.52 percent at 2,637.92 at 0911 GMT while the CAC-40 futures contract was down at 2,644 from 2,661 on Tuesday's close.

Thomson-CSF was down 0.16 percent to 192.70 francs after it reported 1996 net profit of 745 million francs against a 1995 loss of 791 million. Analysts had been expecting a figure as high as 1.2 billion francs.
Thomson, which has an analysts meeting this afternoon, brought forward publication of its results from this evening following a newspaper report giving estimated profits.

The Finance Ministry on Wednesday published a decree in the Official Journal stating the state would keep a special share in the company, 58 percent owned by the state and slated to be privatised. The decree requires any 10 percent change in capital ownership needs to be vetted by the government.
Renault, down 2.54 percent to 138.30, continues recent slide on profit-taking after big jump on plant closure news. Company set to report a big 1996 loss on March 20.
